description: Original Nexal Academy topic checks. These are formative assessments, not official DBE papers.

questions.prompt: What is the highest power of x in a quadratic equation?
questions.explanation: A quadratic has degree 2, so its highest power of x is x².

questions.prompt: Which method is useful when a quadratic factors cleanly?
questions.explanation: Factoring converts the product to zero and lets us use the zero-product property.

questions.prompt: Why can a quadratic have two real solutions?
questions.answer: Its graph can cross the x-axis twice
questions.explanation: The x-intercepts represent solutions, and a parabola may cross the axis at two points.

questions.prompt: What does a solution interval describe?
questions.answer: All values that satisfy the inequality
questions.explanation: An interval collects every input for which the inequality is true.

questions.prompt: When multiplying an inequality by a negative number, what changes?
questions.explanation: Order reverses on the number line when multiplying by a negative.

questions.prompt: Why should critical points be tested in intervals?
questions.answer: The sign can change at a root
questions.explanation: Roots divide the number line into intervals where the expression keeps a constant sign.

questions.prompt: A limit describes the value a function approaches as x approaches what?
questions.explanation: The input moves close to the chosen value, without needing to equal it.

questions.prompt: What is the derivative from first principles based on?
options: A limit of a difference quotient
questions.answer: A limit of a difference quotient
questions.explanation: The difference quotient becomes the derivative as the interval tends to zero.

questions.prompt: Why is factorisation useful before evaluating some limits?
questions.answer: It can remove a common factor causing an indeterminate form
questions.explanation: Cancelling a common factor may reveal the value approached by the simplified expression.

questions.prompt: What is the input of a function commonly called?
questions.explanation: The function maps an input x to an output value.

questions.prompt: What does f(3) mean?
questions.explanation: Function notation evaluates the rule at the specified input.

questions.prompt: How does a vertical translation affect a graph?
questions.answer: It shifts every point up or down
questions.explanation: Adding a constant outside the function changes all y-values by that constant.

questions.prompt: In a right triangle, sin θ equals which ratio?
questions.explanation: Sine compares the side opposite the angle with the hypotenuse.

questions.prompt: Which ratio uses adjacent and hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse.

questions.prompt: Why must the calculator angle mode match the question?
questions.answer: Degrees and radians produce different values
questions.explanation: The same numerical angle has different interpretations in degree and radian measure.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit for acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is change in velocity per second.

questions.prompt: The area under a velocity-time graph represents what?
questions.explanation: Velocity multiplied by time gives displacement; graphically this is area.

questions.prompt: Why is sign convention important in one-dimensional motion?
questions.explanation: A chosen positive direction lets velocity and acceleration signs communicate direction.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: One newton is one kilogram metre per second squared.

questions.prompt: Newton's second law is commonly written as:
questions.explanation: Net force equals mass times acceleration.

questions.prompt: Why do action-reaction forces not cancel on one object?
questions.explanation: Newton's third-law pair is equal and opposite but belongs to two interacting bodies.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of energy?
questions.explanation: A joule is the work done by one newton through one metre.

questions.prompt: Power measures the rate of what?
questions.explanation: Power is energy transferred per unit time.

questions.prompt: What does conservation of energy mean?
questions.answer: Energy is transferred or transformed, not destroyed
questions.explanation: The total energy of an isolated system remains constant.

questions.prompt: What must be conserved when balancing a chemical equation?
questions.answer: The number of atoms of each element
questions.explanation: Atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed.

questions.prompt: A mole is a measure of what?
questions.explanation: One mole contains Avogadro's number of specified particles.

questions.prompt: Why are coefficients changed instead of subscripts when balancing?
questions.answer: Coefficients change quantities without changing identities
questions.explanation: Changing a subscript would describe a different compound.

questions.prompt: What is the sugar in DNA?
questions.explanation: DNA contains deoxyribose; RNA contains ribose.

questions.prompt: Which base pairs with adenine in DNA?
questions.explanation: A pairs with T in DNA through hydrogen bonds.

questions.prompt: Why is DNA replication called semi-conservative?
questions.answer: Each new molecule has one old strand and one new strand
questions.explanation: The original strands act as templates for complementary new strands.

questions.prompt: What is an allele?
questions.answer: An alternative form of a gene
questions.explanation: Alleles occupy the same gene locus but may influence different traits.

questions.prompt: A heterozygous genotype has:
questions.explanation: Heterozygous means the allele pair differs.

questions.prompt: Why can a recessive trait appear when neither parent shows it?
questions.answer: Both parents can carry one recessive allele
questions.explanation: Two carrier alleles can combine in an offspring to form a recessive genotype.

questions.prompt: What is a producer?
questions.answer: An organism that makes its own food
questions.explanation: Plants and algae commonly produce food using light energy.

questions.prompt: Why does available energy decrease up a food chain?
options: Energy is lost as heat and metabolism
Energy is created at each level
questions.answer: Energy is lost as heat and metabolism
questions.explanation: Only part of intake becomes biomass available to the next trophic level.

questions.prompt: How can biodiversity improve ecosystem resilience?
questions.answer: More species provide alternative roles and responses
questions.explanation: Functional variety can help a system recover from disturbance.
